extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, reexamination requesters, and patent practitioners handling reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for processing, filing, amending, assigning, monitoring, and deciding ex parte (and inter partes where noted) reexamination proceedings before the USPTO, per the MPEP and relevant CFR/USC provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locating reexamination file via USPTO public website
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps to find reexamination data on the public USPTO website: go to http://www.uspto.gov → Site Index → letter 'E' → Electronic Business Center → '? Status & View Documents' → select 'Patent Application Information Retrieval' → select 'Patent Number' and enter patent number → Search → Continuity Data → Child Continuity Data lists related reexaminations. Ex parte reexaminations identified by '90' series; inter partes by '95' series. Clicking the reexamination number reveals the 'Contents' for the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter patent number without commas (e.g., 5806063). Use the Continuity Data/Child Continuity Data to locate related reexamination numbers and click hyperlinked reexamination number to view contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locating reexamination file via USPTO intranet (PALM)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the USPTO intranet (http://ptoweb/ptointranet/index.htm) staff can click 'PALM' → 'General Information', enter the patent number in the 'Patent #' box → Search → when Patent Number Information appears, click 'Continuity Data' to obtain the reexamination number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There may be about a ten (10) day lag between filing and data entry into PALM. Use PALM to obtain reexamination number and subsequent status information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Under reexamination there are fees for the request (37 CFR 1.20(c)(1)), for addition of claims (excess claim fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4)), for extension of time, and for any appeal, appeal forwarding fee, and oral hearing fees under 37 CFR 41.20(b). No fee is required for issuance of the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions relating to a reexamination proceeding require fees (37 CFR 1.17(m), 1.20(a)(6) and (a)(7)). Small entity and micro entity reductions are available for certain fees (request, petition, excess claim fees, appeal, appeal forwarding, oral hearing). When a fee is required in a merged proceeding, only a single fee is required (see MPEP §§ 2283, 2285).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of transmittal form for mailings
rubrics_metrics.description: A transmittal form with the requester's address will be used to forward copies of Office actions (and any references cited) to the requester; a copy of this form will be attached to each Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the patent owner is the requester, no such transmittal form is needed. The transmittal form removes the need to retype the requester's address for each mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.530 (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)–(j) and are formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b), and contain all required fees, are entered in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and timing of submitting proposed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed amendment is made by filing a paper directing the proposed specified changes to the patent specification, including the claims, or to the drawings. An amendment paper may accompany a request by the patent owner under § 1.510(e), be part of a patent owner statement under paragraph (b) of § 1.530, or be submitted where permitted during prosecution under § 1.550(a) or § 1.937.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment papers must follow the formal filing rules and can be submitted at specific permitted times in the reexamination process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendments: full-paragraph requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification other than to the claims must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph including markings per paragraph (f), except that an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presenting the text of the paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The precise point in the specification where an added or rewritten paragraph is located must be identified. This applies to paper or compact disc submissions (see §§ 1.96 and 1.825). See MPEP § 2250 for examples of proper claim amendment format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendments: full-text and marking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each patent claim being proposed to be changed and of each new claim being proposed to be added. For any claim changed, a parenthetical 'amended,' 'twice amended,' etc., should follow the claim number. Each changed or added claim must include markings pursuant to paragraph (f), except a canceled claim may be canceled by a statement without presenting its text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each patent claim proposed to be changed and each proposed added claim must include the required markings. All amended claims must be presented as full copies in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendments: sketch and labeling rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on separate paper showing proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner. Upon approval, only new sheets including the changes and in compliance with § 1.84 must be filed. Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended,' added figures as 'New,' and canceled figures must be surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow § 1.84 for drawing sheet format; submit sketches in red to show proposed changes and await examiner approval before filing replacement sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for reexamination papers (1.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal requirements for papers making up the reexamination proceeding other than those in § 1.530 are set out in § 1.52.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all papers meet § 1.52 formatting and content rules in addition to reexamination-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims and support for claim changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims pursuant to paragraph (d), supply on pages separate from the pages containing the changes the status (i.e., pending or canceled) as of the date of the amendment of all patent claims and all added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes to the claims made by the amendment paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, separate pages showing claim status and specific disclosure support for each change to satisfy § 1.530(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking convention for showing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reexamined which are made to the specification, including the claims, must include the following markings: (1) matter to be omitted must be enclosed in brackets; (2) matter to be added must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistently use brackets for deletions and underlining for additions per § 1.530(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of claim numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. The numbering of any claims added in the reexamination proceeding must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure new claim numbers sequentially follow the existing highest claim number and do not renumber existing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment to disclosure may be required for correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to amend the disclosure to bring claims, specification, and drawings into substantial correspondence when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments made relative to the patent as of the request filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments must be made relative to the patent specification, including the claims and drawings, which are in effect as of the date of filing the request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference the patent text as it existed on the request filing date when preparing amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope; no new matter; expired patent restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent. Moreover, no amendment, other than cancellation of claims, will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not propose claim amendments that broaden scope or introduce subject matter not originally disclosed; after expiration only claim cancellations may be incorporated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not legally effective until issuance of reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Office actions will treat proposed amendments as though they have been entered, the proposed amendments will not be effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that prosecution may proceed treating amendments as entered for examination, but legal effect attaches only on issuance and publication of the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFW reexamination amendment entry format (A–G)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an IFW reexamination file, amendments are entered as follows: (A) amendment paper designated by consecutive letters (A, B, C, etc.); (B) each entry blocked by two lines and given successive numbers (A1, A2, ...); (C) copy of claims filed with the request and patent pages containing revised paragraphs printed from IFW file history; (D) a line drawn through any claim(s) or paragraph(s) amended with substituted copy indicated by amendment letter/number; (E) canceled claims/paragraphs part of the patent surrounded by brackets (not lined through); (F) marked up copy of claims filed with the request and patent pages scanned into IFW file history; (G) marked up amendment document scanned into IFW file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow IFW-specific formatting and scanning/entry procedures; claims must not be renumbered; numbering of claims added during reexamination must follow the highest numbered patent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: All amendments must present full copy of amended claims and paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: ALL amendments in reexamination proceedings, including examiner’s amendments made at the time the NIRC is prepared, must be presented in the form of a full copy of the text of each claim which is amended and each paragraph of the description which is amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the entire claim or paragraph text for any amendment; partial fragments are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple successive amendments must show all changes relative to current patent text
rubrics_metrics.description: If a portion of the text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate ALL of the changes (insertions and deletions) in relation to the current text of the patent under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each subsequent amendment must be prepared against the currently effective reexamination text, showing cumulative changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination file data and status codes in PALM and IFW
rubrics_metrics.description: PALM retrieval transactions obtain data on reexamination files; reexamination e-File papers may be viewed on IFW. PALM provides information on patent owner, requester, contents, status, and related Office proceedings. Reexamination proceedings have status codes in the '400' range (some inter partes documents/actions in '800' range), while patent applications have status codes from '020' upward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PALM/IFW to monitor contents and status; be aware of the different status-code ranges for reexamination vs. regular applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent file location control for paper files
rubrics_metrics.description: Movement of paper patent files related to reexamination requests is monitored by PALM. The patent file will be charged to the examiner assigned the reexamination and kept in the examiner's office until conclusion; after conclusion the patent file is forwarded with the reexamination file to OPLA for review and then to Office of Data Management and Record Room after printing of the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely forwarding of paper files at conclusion for certificate printing and record storage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting major events to PALM
rubrics_metrics.description: During processing, major pre-ex parte and ex parte phase events are reported to PALM via the reexamination icon/window in PALM EXPO. Events include: determination mailed—denial; determination mailed—grant; petition for reconsideration received; decision on petition mailed—denied; decision on petition mailed—granted; owner response (owner's statement) received; requester response received; mailing of all examiner actions; receipt of owner responses and Office receipt dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of these events and additional events reported by Preprocessing Unit are permanently recorded and displayed in the 'Contents' portion of PALM; corresponding status representatives are also displayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM automated weekly reports and time thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of automated PALM reports are provided weekly to TCs to indicate approaching deadlines and potential problems. Identified reports include: Requests Not Yet Received in CRU; Requests Not Yet Assigned to an Examiner (report items where 6 weeks since filing); Requests Which Should Be Taken Up for Determination (6th week past); Requests for Which Determinations Should be Prepared (2nd month since filing); Requests for Which Determinations Should Have Been Mailed (10th week since filing); Overdue Determinations (3rd month since filing — should always be zero); Overdue Petitions for Reconsideration of a Denial (6 weeks since determination mailed); Determinations where owner hasn't filed response (10 weeks since mailing); Overdue Requester Responses to Statements (10 weeks since owner response); Overdue First Ex Parte Actions (6 weeks since available for prosecution); Overdue Action or Examiner's Answer (2 months since owner response to previous action); Overdue Advisory Action (1 month since owner response to previous final action); Overdue Owner Response (4 months since action); Overdue Certificates (3 months since NIRC mailed and no issue date); Requests With Prolonged Prosecution (15 months since filing). Items marked with an asterisk require immediate action and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor these reports and take immediate action on starred/overdue items to ensure reexaminations are processed with 'special dispatch' per 35 U.S.C. 305.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of reexamination to art unit and examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination requests should normally be assigned to the CRU art unit which examines the technology (Chemical, Electrical, Mechanical, etc.) in which the patent is classified. The CRU SPRS will assign the request to a primary examiner other than the examiner who originally examined the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment to the original examiner is generally precluded; assign to an examiner most familiar with claimed subject matter. In rare cases where the original examiner is the only knowledgeable examiner, CRU Director approval is required and that approval must be stated in the decision on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner assignment exclusions and conferee participation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination request will not be assigned to an examiner who was involved in any part of the examination of the patent for which reexamination is requested (e.g., prepared/signed an action), or who was involved in the examination of the parent. This excludes conferees who participated in preparing the earlier Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an earlier reexamination is still ongoing, the same examiner may be assigned the new reexamination despite the general exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-pending reissue and reexamination assignment and merger rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is pending and a reexamination request is filed (or vice versa), assignment rules depend on whether reexamination is ordered and whether proceedings are merged by OPLA. If merged, the merged proceeding will generally be handled by the TC examiner handling the reissue after files return from OPLA, except where that examiner was involved in prior examination of the patent, in which case a different examiner will be assigned. If not merged, OPLA will provide guidance on assignment depending on facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TC QAS should notify OPLA promptly when proceedings are ready for consideration of merger; hand-deliver paper files to OPLA when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and remedy for inadvertent assignment to original examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination is inadvertently assigned to an 'original examiner', the patent owner or third-party requester who objects must promptly file a paper alerting the Office within two months of the first Office action or communication indicating the examiner assignment. Reassignment will be addressed case-by-case and assignment alone is not grounds to vacate Office decisions or restart reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the paper directed to examiner assignment has no right of entry under the rules, the Office may waive the rules to enter and consider the paper. Timeliness (two-month window) is critical for objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer procedure for reexaminations between art units
rubrics_metrics.description: If the SPRS to whose art unit a reexamination has been assigned believes it should be assigned to another art unit, the SPRS must obtain consent of the CRU SPRS of the desired unit and hand-carry any paper patent file to that CRU SPRS. Any conflict not resolved by SPRSs will be resolved by the CRU Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers should be handled expeditiously consistent with 35 U.S.C. 305 special dispatch requirement; if the new art unit accepts assignment, its CRU SPRS assigns the request to an examiner in that unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time reporting for reexamination activities
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO personnel must report all time expended on reexamination activities on their individual Time and Attendance Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include activities such as supervision, copying, typing, and docketing when reporting time to ensure accurate workload accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-initiated reexamination authority and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.520 the Director may, at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent, determine whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised by patents or printed publications discovered by the Director or brought to his attention, and may initiate ex parte reexamination without a request and without fee; such orders are rare and only in compelling circumstances after review of all facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to order reexamination at the Director's initiative is delegated to the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy and others specified. If an employee becomes aware of unusual facts, forward a memorandum setting forth facts (including a proposed rejection of claims) with the patent file and prior art to OPLA through supervisory chain; include an electronic disk copy of the memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: No record if Deputy Commissioner refuses to order Director-initiated reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy refuses to issue an order for reexamination, no record of consideration will be maintained in the patent file or elsewhere, and the patent owner will not be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that a refusal leaves no trace in the official file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's statutory decision timeline and record (35 U.S.C. 303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months following filing of a request for reexamination under section 302 the Director will determine whether a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim is raised by the request, with or without consideration of other patents/printed publications. The determination is placed in the official file and a copy mailed to the owner of record and the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence of an SNQ is not precluded by the cited reference having been previously considered by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determination timeline and appeal/petition rights (37 CFR 1.515)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months following filing of an ex parte reexamination request, an examiner will consider the request and determine whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised by the request and prior art cited therein. Statements under § 1.501(a)(2) will not be considered by the examiner in making the determination. The determination is based on claims in effect at the time, becomes part of the official file, and is mailed to the patent owner and requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no SNQ is found, a partial fee refund may be made under § 1.26(c). The requester may seek review by petition to the Director under § 1.181 within one month of mailing of the examiner’s determination; the petition must comply with § 1.181(b). If no timely petition is filed or if the petition affirms no SNQ, the determination is final and nonappealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation search requirement prior to examiner determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a determination on the request for reexamination, the examiner must request a litigation search from Technical Support Staff (TSS) of the CRU or the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) to check if the patent has been or is involved in litigation. The 'Litigation Review' box on the reexamination IFW file jacket form (RXFILJKT) should be completed to indicate the review and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the litigation search and the reexamination file jacket form are scanned into the IFW reexamination file history. If the record or litigation search indicates additional information is desirable, guidance may be obtained from the Office of the Solicitor library. If a paper referring to a court proceeding has been filed, it should be referenced appropriately in the reexamination file.
